claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (presbyter) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius was active during the first half of the fifth century, with Theophanes Confessor recording him as presbyter at Jerusalem in 412.
Hesychius died around 450 or in the 450s, though the exact date is uncertain.
The work Homilia I in sanctum pascha (Homily 1 on Holy Pascha) is also known as homilia 3 in the manuscript tradition.
The homily survives in Greek manuscript, specifically from codex Sinaiticus gr. 492.
The homily was written for the Paschal celebration in the Church, addressing the mystery of Christ's death and resurrection.
Hesychius was renowned as a preacher and theologian, and his Paschal homilies represent part of his celebrated preaching output.
Hesychius played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ and was involved in the theological disputes of his era, including opposition to Nestorianism.
Hesychius was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture and was recognized by 429 as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
The homily addresses themes including the cross as victory, Christ's resurrection, and the defeat of death, with extensive praise of the cross.
Hesychius is not to be confused with Bishop Hesychius of Jerusalem, a contemporary of Gregory the Great.
The homily is catalogued as CPG 6567 in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum.
